From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, lauren_bishop@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, dylan_brooks@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 5 Jan 2027 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: INTERNAL: draft capacity + unit-econ notes for Acme QBR (attached)

Team — I put together an initial worksheet (capacity_model_v1.xlsx) with the following sketches; these are draft numbers to iterate on before we send Elena the packet:

- Baseline assumptions:
  • Baseline tokens/month: 420M (from Elena)
  • Peak factor: 4.5x (99th hr) for launches, diurnal 2.8x spikes
  • Default runtime: fp16 with 16GB KV cache per slot

- GPU economics (monthly effective):
  • Reserved slot (NVIDIA A10x-like) effective cost: $7,200/month (amortized + infra)
  • Burst/spot hourly effective: $18/hour (pre-quantization)
  • Token throughput per slot (avg): 1.8M tokens/hour (depends on sequence len)

- Utilization targets and impact:
  • Target steady-state util: 65–75% to meet p99 SLA headroom
  • Burst headroom: maintain 10–15% spare slots for unexpected surges

- Batching & caching levers:
  • Batching increases throughput (up to +40% tokens/sec under steady workloads) but raises p99 by ~120–200ms depending on queueing window
  • Strict KV cache TTL reduction (from 30min->5min) reduces redundancy and costs on repeated prefixes but increases cold-start token work

Questions for Marissa/Dylan: can you validate the slot throughput numbers by model family and confirm the current observed p99 uplift when batching is enabled (we need empirical numbers tied to sequence-length histogram).

Attachment: capacity_model_v1.xlsx (contains worked examples: committed vs burst mixes and cost per 1M tokens under several configs).

Thanks —
Karthik
Director, Compute Economics

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, lauren_bishop@redwood.com, dylan_brooks@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 6 Jan 2027 14:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: INTERNAL: draft capacity + unit-econ notes for Acme QBR (attached)

On Tue, 5 Jan 2027 at 10:03, Karthik Iyer wrote:
> Team — I put together an initial worksheet (capacity_model_v1.xlsx) with the following sketches...

Quick validation and operational ask:
- Slot throughput: for the models Acme runs (gpt-small variants), observed avg throughput is closer to 2.1M tokens/hr per slot at sequence length ~48; p99 impact with batching (aggressive low-latency batching) is +140ms on average (peak conditions saw +210ms).
- Batching defaults: we can present two recommended profiles in the packet:
  1) Latency-first profile — maintain batching window <= 10ms, modest batching gains (~+12% throughput).
  2) Cost-first profile — batching window 50-80ms, throughput +35–40% but p99 increases ~150–200ms.
- KV caching levers: TTL=30m (current) reduces work by ~28% for interactive prefixes; dropping to 5m reduces that benefit to ~8% but is cheaper when traffic is highly diverse.

Operational proposal for QBR packet:
- Include a contingency plan: canary reserved commit covering 50% of predicted steady-state, automatic burst pool for 2x remaining headroom in us-west.
- Canary rollout notes attached (canary_rollout_notes.md) — includes rollback thresholds (p99>900ms or error rate >1.5%).

I'll prepare the quick tradeoff table with numbers for cost per 1M tokens under the three profiles (Reserved-heavy, Hybrid, Cost-optimized).

Marissa
VP, Serving Platform
